text:
Erik Karlsson is 36, a three-time Norris winner, and the most talked-about defenseman on the trade market. This week's headlines ran from Yardbarker calling him "likely gone by deadline" to reports linking Carolina and Toronto, while Karlsson, per one headline, says there's "Nothing Strange About That."

On the ice he's doing what he always does: 19 points in 20 games, 10 of them on the power play, in 23:38 a night. The quieter worry is at even strength, where Pittsburgh gets only 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there. Some of the light production lately is bad luck, though: the Penguins have scored 4.6 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, and that tends to swing back.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking still has him among the best setup men at his position, 98th percentile in primary shot assists, and Evolving-Hockey had him 23rd of 215 defensemen by wins above replacement last season. Whoever is calling Kyle Dubas is shopping for a power-play quarterback, not a project.
headline: Karlsson keeps passing while the rumors circle
